messages:
sam (support): FYI escalation from Ash at Shoply — sudden p99 jump and a bunch of 503/401 auth bounces starting ~2026-03-16T09:12Z. Customer reports timeouts 10–25s and lots of "auth failure" in response. Request id from one sample: req_0a9c4f7e. Repro curl included below.

maya (support): Copy — can you paste the curl & logs? Is this Dedicated or Hosted?

li (acct-manager): Dedicated (eu-west pool pinned). Customer says problem started after their midday traffic surge. They were on Dedicated pool d-ed-42, min_pool=0, burst allowed.

sam (support): curl they ran:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-shoply-xxxx" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"input":"hello","request_id":"req_0a9c4f7e"}' 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response: intermittent 503 {"error":"auth backend timeout"} or 200 after 18s.

ops-bot: [ALERT] p99 latency spike detected: service=dedicated-serve eu-west pool=d-ed-42 start=2026-03-16T09:10:45Z p95=2.3s p99=19.6s queue_len=214 -> alert_id=ALRT-8721

jonas (eng-sre): Looking at infra metrics now. Initial observation: pool d-ed-42 had attach queue growth at ~09:11 and GPU utilization jumped to ~98%. Provisioner showed cold-attach ramp — several nodes in 'provisioning' for 45s. Kernel image pulls spiked. Could be thundering attach during burst and auth timeouts are downstream effect (request queueing -> auth TTL).

priya (eng-runtime): Also seeing a spike in model load latencies. KV cache hits dropped (cache warm miss) for that model variant. There are concurrent attach fanout events to the same model shard. Min_pool=0 means we rely on autoscale warmup, which can cause cold GPU starts under a sharp burst.

maya (support): Customer says they didn't change anything. They hit a traffic pattern (campaign). They need immediate mitigation and a plan to prevent recurrence.

jonas (eng-sre): Immediate mitigations we can try (rolling):
- Route traffic for Shoply to a reserved warm pool (hot-pool) if we can map their org id -> route.
- Temporarily set min_pool=2 for their Dedicated pool to keep GPUs warm.
- Bump fairshare priority for their queue to reduce attach fanout.
- Fallback policy: route excess to Hosted endpoint (with conservative rate limit & same model) to avoid client errors.

priya (eng-runtime): I can do min_pool change and set routing fallback. Maya, can you get Customer org id & permission to change? I will also throttle attach parallelism and enable prefetch warmup for that org.

li (acct-manager): I have permission. Apply min_pool=2 and enable hosted fallback — customer agrees.

sam (support): Actioning now: applying min_pool=2 on d-ed-42 for org shoply_id=org_772. Also enabling hosted fallback for that org.

infra-bot: Completed: set_min_pool d-ed-42 org_772 -> 2 (applied by priya).

ops-bot: Route update: shoply_id=org_772 fallback -> hosted:enabled.

jonas (eng-sre): After changes I see queue shrink and p99 drop from ~19s -> ~3.1s over 2 minutes. Auth error rate fell to baseline. Good sign. Need follow-ups: investigate why provisioner delayed (image-pull/backoff?), reduce cold-attach penalty.

priya (eng-runtime): Found provisioning logs for node attach ramp: several nodes timed out during image pull from registry due to a transient registry throttle. That delayed attach by ~30–60s. We'll add image pull caching on workers and increase registry client retries/backoff jitter.

maya (support): Customer reports degraded but usable. They appreciate the fallback and setting. Ash (customer) — can you confirm traffic is back to normal on your side?

ash (customer): Confirmed. p99 much improved, errors stopped after the routing change. Thanks, team.

sam (support): Postmortem TODOs (short):
- P0: image-pull caching + registry retry improvements (eng-infra).
- P1: default min_pool policy for Dedicated customers with non-zero traffic history (product + eng-runtime).
- P2: improve autoscale warmup prefetch for org-scoped warm caches.
- P2: provide support runbook to quickly set min_pool & enable hosted fallback.

jonas (eng-sre): I'll open infra ticket with traceID list and attach provisioning timelines. Also adding a short mitigation script to atomically set min_pool + route fallback.

li (acct-manager): I'll follow up with Shoply and confirm long-term SLA changes & offer guidance on reserved capacity.

maya (support): Thanks all. Marking this thread closed for now; will update when tickets are in. :white_check_mark:
